question: Pasta water salted at 10 g per litre: by how many °C does its boiling point rise?
move: Before crediting a small ingredient with a big effect, work out how big the effect really is.
ask: Before I credit a tiny thing with a big effect, have I checked how big it really is?
trap: Believing salted water boils hotter enough to cook pasta faster.
hint: Salt weighs 58.4 g per mole and splits in two; count particles, then use water's boiling constant, 0.512 °C per mole per kg.
steps: 10 g / 58.4 g per mole = 0.171 mol of salt in 1 kg of water.
Each unit splits into 2 ions: 0.171 x 2 = 0.342 mol of particles.
Each mole of particles per kg lifts water's boiling point 0.512 °C.
reference: Atkins & de Paula, Atkins' Physical Chemistry, 8th edition, Oxford University Press, 2006
